kb/Work PB3338 (wave 1154) and PB3540 (wave 1157): the APPLY COMMIT clause, COMMIT and ROLLBACK are provided for RELATIVE and INDEXED files, whose keyed store engine keeps the transaction (kb/Work PB3337); a SEQUENTIAL or LINE SEQUENTIAL file named in the clause is under commit control too, its transaction journal being kb/Work PB3340 (COBOLNET1709, which refused it, is retired) (Annex A.4.3 stays PARTIAL, docs/CONFORMANCE.md 5; this rule's obligations are met for every file the clause admits). GR3: an activation under the control of a recursive runtime element raises EC-FLOW-APPLY-COMMIT (Table 13's name for GR3/GR4's 'EC-FLOW-APPLY') under the ACTIVATING element's checking, latched by ProgramTable.CallProgram, and with checking off the clause stays inactive. A recursive runtime element (8.6.6: a RECURSIVE program, a function, a method) is a frame the module stack marks recursive, whatever pushed it: ProgramTable.CallProgram and ActivateMain for a program or function, the emitted method body (OoEmitter.EmitMethod) for a method, and TransactionControl.FlowForbidden asks ModuleStack.AnyRecursive, so an activation a method causes is forbidden like one a RECURSIVE program causes. Compiled paths: pb3338_ec_flow_apply_commit_under_recursive_element (a RECURSIVE program) and pb3540_ec_flow_apply_commit_under_method (a method), each CALLing an element with a clause with checking on at the CALL (the condition, the activation not made) and off (no condition, the clause inactive). Below 2023 the clause is refused (pb3540_commit_under_method_below_2023). retired-witness: conformance:wiseowl/cases/12.4.6.3-APPLY-COMMIT/declined-apply-commit (the commit and rollback facility is provided for the keyed organizations (kb/Work PB3338): the decline these witnessed is gone, and the rule is now witnessed by its own implementation) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Validation/DeclinedFacilityPass.cs#VisitApplyCommitClause (the commit and rollback facility is provided for the keyed organizations (kb/Work PB3338): the decline these witnessed is gone, and the rule is now witnessed by its own implementation) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/ProgramTable.cs#AnyRecursiveActive (kb/Work PB3540: the recursion question is the run unit's module stack's (ModuleStack.AnyRecursive), because a method is a frame there and no ProgramTable node; the table's own query, which could not see a method, is deleted)

kb/Work PB319 LANDED, after kb/Work PB316 (landed). ONE SITE, FULL ANTECEDENT. The rule (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3, both its leading conjunct and its two disjuncts: OK, rule 8) is a syntax rule of the OPEN STATEMENT about file-name-1, which 14.9.27.2's general format defines as that statement's operand; 12.4.5.15.3 has exactly ONE general rule and NO syntax rules, so SR8 is the standard's only source of a LOCK MODE requirement anywhere. It was enforced in TWO places. The second copy, in DataBinder.BindFileControl, fired off the SELECT clause alone and had to DROP the antecedent, because a file control entry sees no OPEN statement and the I-O-CONTROL paragraph is not bound until after it. That copy is DELETED (the extraction IS the fix), leaving StatementValidation.CheckOpenSharingAllOther, called from BindOpen once per file-name, as SR8's only site; its two disjuncts collapse onto the effective sharing mode 'sharing ?? file.Sharing' (14.9.27.4 GR23), which after PB316 is the file's OWN open group's phrase. MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER on this worktree's cobol.exe at --std 2002. sr8ovr.cob (SELECT F1 ...
